last_session.detail: They arrived at sunset. They assumed the treasure lay at one of the marked locations, though all the surrounding land was unknown to them.
last_session.text: The party arrived in Brandonsford following a treasure map whose marked places they did not recognize.

last_session.detail: Reginald is a frog at the river. He said the Clurichen is up to no good and that wherever it goes, they should stay away.
last_session.text: Reginald the frog warned Dr. Uriah that a trickster Clurichen comes into town from the riverbanks nightly.

last_session.detail: Dunk split from the party, preferring solitude to the inns, to scavenge at the farm on the edge of town. Gill's legend: Sir Brandon met a fairy in the woods who gave him a magic sword; he and his friends killed a dragon that had terrorized the town for weeks, and the town was named after him. They were knighted, then left, and Brandon died. That dragon was dragged through town and ripped apart hundreds of years ago; Gill assumes the current one is different and does not know where dragons come from. Gill saw the current dragon and sent his three sons after it. Dunk asked to sleep in the barn and think over the offer; they drank from Gill's still while Gill shared gossip.
last_session.text: Dunk got drunk with Farmer Gill, who told how Sir Brandon slew the town's dragon centuries ago.

last_session.detail: Eric said the dragon was the first of many problems he has. He says George, a capable woodsman living a couple of houses down who might come to the tavern, lost an arm to the dragon and described it as a black dragon, not a big one; George does not know where his arm is. Eric defended George's account; the duel was set for dawn, but the flustered Eric only said Sir Phidipaldi was more skilled at adventure and did not accept.
last_session.text: Eric the Reeve offered 1000 gold for the dragon. Sir Phidipaldi then slapped him with a glove and challenged him to a duel.

last_session.detail: Uriah bought him a Fox Tail Brew; Ned recognized Uriah as a Dagonite. Uriah said he was a scholar of folk remedies and lore looking for work with his crew. Ned asks 100 gold for the week; for a night of at least ten kills he would keep the fee but give back 5 gold per kill if he could do what he wanted with the victims. Uriah said he would think about it.
last_session.text: Drop Dead Ned, a thief with a killer wasp, offered to hire on with Dr. Uriah.

last_session.detail: Quinn says however much good stock he buys, it is gone by morning with half the glasses empty or knocked over, so he waters down what he has. He suspects Bentley because Bentley's Fox Tail Brew is so popular. Quinn offered 100 gold and proposed a fake shipment, which Sir Phidipaldi agreed to stage.
last_session.text: Sir Phidipaldi agreed to help Quinn of the Golden Egg catch whoever empties his ale each night.

open.detail: The party does not recognize the map's marked locations.
open.text: Find the treasure shown on the party's map.

open.detail: Sir Phidipaldi said they would talk to the Reeve, then denied the dragon exists and challenged Eric to a duel.
open.text: Kill the black dragon and drag its body into Brandonsford for Eric the Reeve's 1000 gold. The party never clearly accepted.

open.detail: The ale vanishes from the Golden Egg each night.
open.text: Catch whoever empties Quinn's good ale each night and collect his 100 gold.

open.detail: Lady Hilda is a seasoned fighter in chain mail with a shield.
open.text: If the party pays Lady Hilda, she will join them to hunt the dragon. She won't go alone.

open.detail: Dr. Uriah said he would think about it.
open.text: If Dr. Uriah hires Drop Dead Ned for 100 gold a week, Ned and his killer wasp will do any job. Ned insists on killing people.

open.detail: Quinn brings bottles, they fill them with water, and Sir Phidipaldi makes a big show of delivering ale to the Golden Egg.
open.text: If Sir Phidipaldi and Quinn stage their fake ale delivery, they may see who comes for the ale.
Where are the map's marked places, and which holds the treasure?

open.detail: Half the glasses are left empty or knocked over. Quinn believes Bentley is stealing it.
open.text: Who or what empties Quinn's good ale each night?
Where does the black dragon lurk outside Brandonsford?

open.detail: Bentley's restocking shipment is a week overdue, and nothing has come into Brandonsford in months.
open.text: What happened to Bentley's shipment, and why has nothing reached Brandonsford?

open.detail: Sir Brandon's dragon was killed centuries ago and none has appeared since. Farmer Gill does not know where dragons come from.
open.text: Where did the new dragon come from?
